newsitem.title: CHINA: Multinationals lower China profit expectations.
newsitem.headline: Multinationals lower China profit expectations.

text.p: Multi-national firms are scaling down their profitability estimates for business in China, but there is no sign of any reduction of investment in the Chinese market, an industry consultant said on Thursday.
William Best, Asian vice-president for consultancy A.T. Kearney, said his firm's latest annual survey of 67 multi-nationals operating in China showed a dramatic downturn in expectations.

"Previously, multi-nationals operating in China, when asked how long they expected it would be before they broke even, would say two-to-three years. But this time, it is more like five-to-six years," Best said in a telephone interview.
"Clearly reality is setting in with regard to the difficulties of operating in China," he added.

At the same time, investment by multi-nationals is still growing. The companies surveyed on average have four joint ventures or wholly-owned enterprises each in operation in China, and expect to add another six in the next five years.
"The additional amount planned to be invested in China over the next five years is twice that already invested and committed," the survey said.
"People continue to look at China as a market that everyone has to be in. It is the second-to-last great market growth opportunity, the other one being India," Best said.
The survey indicated the biggest problem faced by foreign multi-nationals operating in the China market continues to be finding the right people to manage and staff their operations.
But a previous major difficulty -- lack of knowledge and understanding of the China market -- has dropped down the list.
